flagged.title: Telescopes: Optics, Magnification and Resolution
flagged.reason: The video states the 39 m ELT collects around 200,000 times more light than the human eye instead of 30 million, which is mathematically wrong by two orders of magnitude and teaches an incorrect figure that undermines the light grasp formula.

mark_affecting.quote: To put that in perspective, that means it will collect around 200,000 times more light than your naked eye.

flagged.title: Space Probes and Crewed Exploration
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly states that both Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 flew by all four gas giants, which would lead students to incorrectly identify Voyager 1 as visiting Uranus and Neptune.

mark_affecting.quote: Launched way back in 1977, they flew by all four gas giants

flagged.title: The Milky Way and Other Galaxies
flagged.reason: The video hedges using the old error by stating the Milky Way has loose arms and sits between SBb and SBc, whereas the GCSE specification and exam questions strictly require SBb.

mark_affecting.quote: Because of our highly distinct central bar of stars and relatively loose arms, the Milky Way sits right on the fence between an SBb and an SBc classification.
